card st-build-implement-search  [decided]
A builder pass gets the index of decided cards, and searches the map before it decides what no cited card gives
why: The cited cards and their closure miss decisions that sit in another branch of the map. A builder that cannot see such a card decides the question again and contradicts it.

Beside its input, each pass gets the id and the title of every decided card in the map. Before the pass decides a question that no cited card answers, it searches the titles, the whys and the bodies of the map for the terms of the question, and reads every card that matches. A decided card that answers the question binds the pass the same as a cited card. Only a search that finds no answer leads to a proposed card (#st-build-missing-decision).

  -> refines         st-build-implement  The implement step: a fresh agent runs the /implement skill on the ticket
  -> depends_on      st-build-missing-decision  A builder that hits a decision no card makes proposes it, builds on the proposal, and the person rules after the fact
       why: The search runs before the proposal that #st-build-missing-decision defines, and an empty search is what allows that proposal.
  <- alternative_to  st-build-implement-search:opt0  Add the refines children of every card in the cited closure to the input
  <- alternative_to  st-build-implement-search:opt1  Keep the input as it is and add the missing depends_on edges where a gap shows
  <- depends_on      werk-cli-search  `werk search` prints the index of decided cards, or the cards whose words match every term
Options
  st-build-implement-search:opt0  Add the refines children of every card in the cited closure to the input
    why not: It finds a decision only when that decision is a child of a closure card. A decision two branches away stays out of reach, and the input fills with cards that do not apply to the ticket.
  st-build-implement-search:opt1  Keep the input as it is and add the missing depends_on edges where a gap shows
    why not: It repairs one case after it fails, and the next missing edge opens the same gap.

The builder's prompt now makes it check that a card is new before it proposes one. The prompt tests pass. I did not run the full check suite. I also have not seen a real build pass behave differently.

The prompt is built in `src/build-prompt.ts`. It already told the builder to search the map before it decides something. It did not tell the builder to search again before it adds a card. These changes close that gap:

- **Before each card:** The builder writes the rule as one sentence. It runs at least two searches with different words. It reads every matching decided card and every card this ticket already proposed.
- **When to skip the card:** If a card already states the rule or implies it, the builder proposes nothing. The same applies when the new card only adds a detail, a value, an exception, or a narrower case. The builder records the existing card with a `followed` entry instead.
- **When to propose:** The `--why` must name the nearest existing card and say what it leaves open. The builder links to that card and does not copy its content.
- **Decision pass:** The same two-search rule and the "implied rule" check apply there.

I added a test in `src/build-prompt.test.ts` for the new wording.

The rule for the card #st-build-implement-search covers the first search only. It does not cover the check before a proposal. Next: propose a change to #st-build-implement-search so the card matches the new prompt.
